turns.text: The elders want everyone at the main hall for the evening meal.
Everyone? Even the cousins from the border post?
Even them. It must be important. Or someone's birthday.
Who's sweeping the clan gate this week?
You are. I did it last week, and the week before.
The crest on the gate needs repainting.
Ask the painters' lane. They did it beautifully last time.
Our clan day's coming. Have you thought about what to bring?
Grandmother's pickles. I'm afraid of what happens if I don't.
The storehouse is full to the rafters.
Then the feast's on. Nothing in an Akimichi storehouse stays full for long.
Another bowl?
I've had four.
That wasn't a question.
A doe gave birth by the stream this morning.
Write it in the book. And leave them both be for a week.
You fell asleep in the forest again.
I was watching clouds. It's clan work, technically.
The kennels need mucking out.
The kennels always need mucking out. That's the whole of the clan's history.
Your partner's been howling at the gate since you left.
Four hours! I was only at the market.
The orchids in the greenhouse opened overnight.
Then the shop window changes today. Bring the ladder.
The hives are calm today.
Good. Calm hives, calm clan.
The garden beds need turning before the fireflies hatch.
Gently. Last year someone dug too deep.
Inspection at the police headquarters tomorrow. Polish your boots.
My boots are always polished.
Polish them again.
The living tree has a new shoot by the hall door.
Then we'll need to move the door. Again.
I brushed the old names on the memorial wall this morning.
All of them?
All of them. Every single one.
You held your guard too high again.
The moon was in my eyes.
The moon will always be in your eyes. Lower it.
The forge was cold when I came in. Who banked it badly?
The apprentice. I've already given the talk.
The shrine wants a new gate before the New Year.
Then the whole yard's on it. Cypress, and no nails.
The racks of willow bark are dry.
Then grind them tonight. The hospital wants fever powder by morning.
Do you ever wish you'd been born outside the clan?
Sometimes. Then I sit at the long table, and I don't.
The elder praised your work at the meeting.
Out loud?
Out loud. In front of everyone. I nearly fell off the bench.
Did you buy the radishes?
I bought a lamp.
We needed radishes.
We needed a lamp. We'll have radishes in the dark otherwise.
Your mother's visiting for the festival.
The whole festival?
The whole festival. And the week after.
The roof's leaking over the futon again.
I'll ask the Kinoshita yard. Again.
You left your kunai on the kitchen table.
I'll move them.
You said that yesterday. And the day before.
The tailor says your jacket can't be mended anymore.
That jacket's been on more missions than most Jonin.
Then let it retire.
Shall we walk down to the river after supper?
Like we used to. Yes, let's.
Twelve years married this spring.
Twelve? I'd have guessed fewer.
That's the kindest thing you've said all year.
You worried while I was away, didn't you?
I reorganised the whole spice shelf.
So yes.
I still have the paper lantern from the night we met.
That old thing? It barely holds a candle.
It holds enough.
I'm sorry about this morning.
So am I. Let's have supper and forget the sharp words.
You're home early!
The mission was quick. The client cried, the cat was found, I came home.
Snow's coming. I can smell it.
Then I'm not leaving this house until spring.
Tea?
Please. You always make it better than I do.
Who's on the gate tonight?
Us. Again. Bring the good tea this time.
The Mission Desk had forty D-ranks come in this morning.
Forty? It's Market Day. Everyone's lost a cat at once.
The new apprentice burnt the rice again.
Third time this week. I'm starting to think it's deliberate.
Did you restock the bandages?
Twice. The Genin go through them like paper.
The boss wants the shelves reorganised by colour.
By colour? What's wrong with by what it is?
Ichiraku's queue went round the corner at lunch.
That's the Academy letting out. Every child in the village had the same idea.
The furniture delivery's late.
The carpenters' lane is buried in orders before the festival. It'll be days.
Fold the towels in thirds, not halves.
Who decided thirds?
The bath house decided thirds. Forty years ago.
I've worked this stall nineteen years.
And still you can't tell a turnip from a radish.
I can. I just like hearing you correct me.
You stayed after shift again.
The ledger wouldn't balance. I can't sleep when it won't balance.
Thank you for covering for me yesterday.
Your little one was sick. Of course I did.
Busy day.
Busy week. Busy season. I need a holiday.
We're getting one. It's called New Year.
The heat in the kitchen today, I could cook an egg on my forehead.
Don't. We've got enough orders.
Three sprained ankles from the training grounds before noon.
The obstacle course again. They never learn to land.
The herbalists sent the new salve.
Good. It smells like a swamp, but it works.
Count the carts again. I make it twenty-two.
Twenty-three. One's a goat with a basket on its back.
Quiet road today.
Quiet's good. Quiet means our relief comes on time.
Lunch?
Lunch. I thought you'd never ask.
How much for the cabbage?
Three ryo.
Three? It was two last week.
Last week it was smaller.
Is the eel fresh?
It's still moving. You tell me.
Can you hold this jacket till Market Day?
For you, till the day after.
Two bowls of miso, one extra egg.
Who gets the egg?
Whoever argues best.
Do you sell fruit milk?
In the cooler. Strawberry's nearly gone.
I bought this lamp here a year ago. Still working.
Of course it is. I don't sell lamps that give up.
The tea across the street is cheaper.
Then why are you standing in my shop?
Because yours is better. Don't tell them I said so.
Do you have any more of the sesame dango?
Last skewer. It's yours if you're quick.
Long queue at Ichiraku tonight.
Academy graduates. They've been here an hour.
Then I'll wait. It's worth it.
Have you tried the senbei shop in the Uchiha quarter?
Every week. The soy ones. I walk all the way there.
The grocer's got persimmons in.
Already? Then autumn's properly here.
They say the bookshop's got the new card set.
My nephew's been waiting a month. I'd better hurry.
You're buying flowers?
For the hospital. A friend broke an ankle on the climbing cliff.
Cut flowers, then. Never a potted plant for the sick.
Sorry, I've only got a thousand-ryo note.
For a dango? You'll take my whole till in change!
Is it always this busy?
Only on Market Day. And festival days. And every day ending in -day.
Thank you, come again.
I always do.
In our day the market street was a dirt track.
In our day there was no market street. We traded at the well.
That's because you're older than me.
The Hokage Rock had only one face when I was a child.
And now four. I hope I live to see another carved.
The tea house has changed its cups.
Those cups were older than both of us.
Exactly. Some things should stay.
Remember when the river froze solid?
The winter of the long snow. We skated to the farms and back.
The young ones run everywhere now.
We ran everywhere too. We just ran slower.
The cherry tree by the shrine bloomed early.
It always does when the winter's kind. Mark it in the book.
My knees know the rain's coming before the clouds do.
Mine tell me every morning. Whether it rains or not.
I taught three generations of this street to read.
And they all still mind their spelling around you.
I still set out a cup for my husband every morning.
Of course you do. I still talk to my wife's garden.
Do you think we did well by the village?
Look at it. Children laughing, ramen steaming. We did well enough.
Did you hear? The fishmonger's grandchild just made Genin.
That family. Fish and shinobi, fish and shinobi. Never anything in between.
Cold today.
Every day's cold at our age. Sit closer to the brazier.
That young one from the apartments carried my basket all the way home yesterday.
Good manners. The Leaf's raising them right.
The bell rope's fraying.
I'll tell the priests. They never look up.
Another game of go?
You'll only lose again.
That's why I like playing you.
Meet at the bridge for the fireworks?
Bridge at nine. If you're late, I'm eating your candied apple.
You won a goldfish?
I won a goldfish. I have no idea how to keep a goldfish.
You wore the blue yukata.
You said you liked it, the first festival.
I did. I still do.
My net broke on the very first goldfish!
Mine broke before I even touched the water. Let's try target throwing instead.
Fox mask or cat mask?
Fox. Then we can sneak up on the grown-ups.
Did you clean behind the stove?
It's New Year's Eve. I'm not cleaning behind anything.
Last year's dust will follow you into the new one.
What did you wish for at the shrine?
If I tell you, it won't come true.
Then wish for something I can help with next year.
Shall we clear the lane together?
You take the top, I'll take the bottom. Tea at the middle.
How many blossom weeks have we seen?
More than I can count. Each one the first, somehow.
Cushions for the finals, please. Four.
Last four in the stall. You're lucky. The visitors have been buying since dawn.
Watching the finals?
Every match. Taking notes.
For when it's your turn?
For when it's my turn.
How many carts through the gate?
Sixty-one. And a goat.
There's always a goat.
You've got your headband on crooked.
Leave it. Everyone's looking.
That's exactly why I'm fixing it.
Duel by moonlight?
Only if you don't cry when you lose.
You've never once seen me cry.
It's dark. That's why.
Grandmother wants us all for supper on the last day of the month.
All of us? Where will we sit?
On each other, probably. Same as every year.
Did you fix the gate?
I tied it with wire.
That's not fixing, that's hoping.
Our cousin's coming from the farms for Market Day.
Then hide the pickles. Last time the barrel came back empty.
Who's cooking for New Year?
Not you. Never again you. The rice cakes were grey.
Mother's planted chrysanthemums again.
Says it's for the shrine. It's really to beat the neighbour's.
Is the old ladder still in the shed?
The one with the cracked rung? Nobody's been brave enough to throw it out.
You've got your father's laugh. You know that?
Everybody tells me. I wish I'd heard more of it.
I found our old Academy notebooks in the trunk.
Burn them. Please. Mine has a poem in it.
I've already read it to the whole family.
Grandfather still keeps his old headband in the drawer.
Polished every week. Don't ever touch it.
You never call.
I'm right here, every week, at your table.
You never call before you come. That's what I mean.
The baby's teething. Nobody in the house has slept.
I'll take a night. Bring the little one round.
You've grown again!
I'm twenty-four. I stopped growing years ago.
Not to me you didn't.
Your brother passed his exam!
I know. The whole street has heard about it since breakfast.
Supper's at six.
It's always at six.
And you're always late.
Ichiraku tonight?
Ichiraku every night. Why do you even ask anymore?
I finally beat the dango stall's record. Twelve skewers.
And how's your stomach?
We don't talk about my stomach.
Did you see the new tea house across the market? Half the price.
Half the tea, too. I'll stay loyal, thanks.
Let's go up the Hokage Rock at sunset.
Last time we did that you got stuck on the third face.
Second face. And it was dark.
The bath house has fruit milk again.
Then my whole evening is decided.
I'm learning to make dumplings. My kitchen looks like a snowstorm.
Bring me the failures. I'm not fussy.
The fishmonger gave me extra eel today.
You must be the favourite. The fishmonger only ever gives me bones.
Did you hear the bell from the shrine at dawn?
Every morning. I've stopped hearing it. Is that sad?
A little. Come and listen with me tomorrow.
Do you ever think about leaving the village? Seeing the coast?
Every time the fish cart comes in. Then I eat the fish and forget.
You've been quiet all week.
Work's heavy. It'll pass.
Then I'll be loud enough for both of us till it does.
I kept the letter you sent when I was laid up with fever.
That silly drawing of the cat?
It's on my wall. Don't you dare laugh.
Thank you for helping me move. My back's still talking to me about it.
Mine too. We'll go to the bath house and complain together.
When did we meet? I can't remember a time before.
The flood year. You lent me a dry pair of sandals.
And you never gave them back.
Rain again! My washing's been out for three days.
Bring it to mine. I've got a line by the stove.
You look tired.
I sat up reading till two. The tea house is my only hope.
Your cooking's improved.
That's the nicest lie anyone's told me all week.
Lovely evening.
It is. Let's just stand here a moment.
Same time tomorrow?
Same time, same bench.
Dare you to touch the Hokage Rock's nose.
You can't even get up there. It's taller than the whole Academy.
I've got two ryo. Dango or a spinning top?
Dango. Then you can spin the stick.
The teacher's got a new chalk board. It squeaks.
Good. Now we'll hear when the questions are coming.
Want to play shinobi and bandits?
I'm the shinobi.
You're always the shinobi!
I saw a deer at the edge of the Nara forest!
Did it see you?
It looked at me like I was boring.
My big sister says ghosts live under the old bridge.
Your big sister says lots of things to make you cry.
Let's catch tadpoles by the river after lessons.
My mother said no more tadpoles in the house.
We'll keep them in a bucket. A secret bucket.
Hide and seek. You count to fifty.
Last time you hid so well we went home.
That's the point!
My dad lets me hold the kunai when he cleans them. The blunt end.
My grandpa lets me sharpen pencils with one. Sort of the same.
I learnt a new hand sign today. Watch.
That's just your fingers crossed.
It's a very advanced hand sign.
Do you think I'll be good at missions?
You found my lost sandal in the river. You're already good at missions.
I don't like the dark.
Me neither. That's why I sleep with the lantern on. Don't tell.
When I grow up I'm opening a ramen stand.
Then I'll eat there every day for free.
Every day for half price. I'll need money.
I miss my cousin. They moved to the farms.
You can write letters. I'll help with the hard words.
It's snowing! It's snowing!
Snowball fight! Last one to the yard is a turnip!
I fell off the climbing frame.
Are you hurt?
Only my feelings. And my knee. Mostly my feelings.
The festival's tonight!
I've saved four ryo. I'm going to win a goldfish.
I got a good mark on the written test!
Really? Show me. ...Wow. I'm telling everyone.
Race you home!
Go!
Your cat was on my roof again.
It thinks your roof is its roof.
It might be right. It's up there more than I am.
Are you using the well this morning?
After you. I'm still finding my sandals.
Who plays the flute at midnight?
The new tenant on the top floor.
Lovely tune. Terrible hour.
I've got too many persimmons. Take a basket.
Again? My whole kitchen is orange.
The stairwell lamp's out again.
I'll bring a candle. I'm not buying another wick, it's your turn.
Lend me a cup of rice? I'll pay you back on Market Day.
You said that last Market Day.
And I paid you back! Mostly.
Your washing's dripping on my step.
Sorry! I'll move the line.
Don't. My step's never been so clean.
The street's having a sweep-out before the festival. Are you in?
If there's tea after, I'm in.
I heard you singing in the bath last night.
The walls are thinner than I thought.
You're better than you think, too.
I've lived on this lane thirty years.
Then you've seen everything.
I've seen everyone. That's better.
I made too much soup.
You always make too much soup.
And you always come and help me eat it.
Did the storm get your fence?
Half of it. The other half is in your garden.
Quiet street tonight.
Everyone's gone to the festival. Shall we sit out on the step?
Your little one waved at me from the window this morning.
Every morning. You're the window friend now.
Someone's been leaving their sandals on the third-floor landing.
A whole tower of them. I counted nine pairs.
The building's water's hot again!
Only took the landlord a month. A festival of a day.
Morning.
Morning. Looks like a fine one.
Have you eaten?
I ate at Ichiraku.
That's not eating. That's slurping. Sit.
Your sensei came by asking for you.
Was I in trouble?
Only for being late. Again.
Take the umbrella.
It's not going to rain.
Take the umbrella.
Help me carry the rice sacks in.
I just got back from a mission!
Then your arms are warmed up.
You left your headband on the washing line.
I was drying it!
It was dry yesterday. It's been there three days.
The neighbours say you've been training at the lake at dawn.
Is that bad?
It's wonderful. Just tell me next time, so I don't worry.
You look more like your grandmother every year.
Is that good?
She was the bravest woman on this street. So yes.
When you were small, you were afraid of the ninken.
I'm still a little afraid of the ninken.
Good. They're very big.
I'm proud of you. I don't say it enough.
You say it every time I leave the house.
Then I'll say it when you come back, too.
Did you want to be a shinobi, or did you just want to make me proud?
Both. Is that allowed?
That's how most of us started.
You're home late.
The mission ran over. I'm fine. Look, all ten fingers.
You've grown out of that jacket.
I like that jacket.
Your elbows like it less. Let's go to the tailor.
Is that a new cut?
Training. It's nothing.
Let me see. Sit down. Let me see.
Go to sleep.
Five more minutes.
You said that an hour ago.
Forty laps this morning.
Forty-one.
You're lying.
Count them yourself tomorrow.
Your shuriken went wide on the third throw.
You were watching? I'm flattered.
I hear you're top of the Mission Desk tally this month.
Jealous?
Motivated.
Rematch. Training ground three. Dawn.
Bring a spare headband. You'll want to hide your face after.
Nice footwork yesterday.
Was that a compliment?
Don't get used to it.
My stall sold more chestnuts than yours today.
Mine sold better chestnuts.
Nobody can taste "better" through the shell.
Your tea's a ryo cheaper than mine again.
And yours is a ryo worse.
Ha! We'll see who's still open in spring.
My garden's chrysanthemums are taller.
Mine have more heads. The judges count heads.
The judges are your cousins.
The tea house has your name above mine on the go board.
Read it again. It's in order of wins.
Why do you always train at the same time as me?
Why do you always train at the same time as me?
...Fair.
You pushed me today. I'll admit that.
I always push you. That's the point of me.
When we were small, I wanted to be you.
And now?
Now I want to beat you. It's healthier.
If you ever leave the village, who'll I compete with?
I'm not going anywhere. Who'd keep you honest?
I can climb the Academy wall faster than you.
Can not.
Can so. Race you.
...Tomorrow. I've got a stitch.
I got a better mark on the throwing test.
By one point.
One point is still a point!
What did the Mission Desk give you?
Weeding. Three gardens. A Chunin, weeding.
Every rank weeds. That's the Leaf.
Back from the east road?
Escort job. The merchant talked the whole way. Every step, every hour.
Have you tried the new kunai from the weapon shop?
Lighter. Flies further, sticks harder. I bought a dozen.
Training ground three's booked till noon.
Then we'll take the lake. Water walking, wet clothes, the usual.
My sensei made us carry logs up the cliff all morning.
Mine made us carry each other. I'd take logs.
Paper bombs went up a ryo at the tool shop.
Powder cart's late. Everything's gone up a ryo.
Who's got the night watch on the wall?
The Tobari, mostly. They can hear a cat land three roofs away.
How long were you out?
Six days. I'd trade my headband for a hot bath.
Did you eat before the spar?
Barbecue. A plate of beef.
Smart. Hits harder for a while after.
You look done in.
Up till three. Couldn't sleep before the mission.
Sleep in your own bed before midnight next time. You wake up with chakra to spare.
Your ninken's getting good at tracking.
Started on the cat-finding D-ranks. Cats leave a strong trail.
Do you ever miss the Academy?
The lunches. Not the tests.
My first C-rank, my hands shook the whole way.
Mine still do. You just learn to throw with them shaking.
I've never once hit the bullseye at the festival target stall.
A Chunin, and you can't win a paper fan?
Chakra's not allowed. That's my excuse.
Our sensei was late again.
Ours too. We practised hand signs for an hour waiting.
Maybe they're all together somewhere, laughing at us.
Two D-ranks today! Painting a fence and catching a goat.
Which was harder?
The fence. The goat had more sense.
Good mission?
Good enough. Home in one piece.
{client} needs those rice sacks carried up to the third floor, and nobody's got the back for it.
I'd help, but my knee. Somebody young ought to give a hand.
Did {neighbor} ever get that roof patched?
Not yet. Another rain like last night and the whole kitchen floods.
{client} has to mind the stall and see to a delivery at the same time.
Can't be done. Someone should offer to watch the counter for an hour.
The firewood's still piled outside {neighbor}'s door. Hasn't been split in a week.
With those hands? It won't be split till spring unless someone helps.
{client} asked me to water the garden while they're away, and I'm off to my sister's tomorrow.
Ask around. Somebody's bound to have an afternoon free.
The shutters on {neighbor}'s house are hanging by one hinge.
I keep meaning to fix them. I don't own a single tool.
{client} has a letter from family far away, but the writing's too small to read anymore.
Someone with young eyes should read it aloud. It's been sitting on the table for days.
Our elder wants the offering taken to the shrine before the next full moon.
The steps are too much for those old legs. We need someone to go in their place.
{client} has a parcel that has to reach {place} today, and can't leave the house.
The Mission Desk would charge a fortune. Maybe someone would just do it as a kindness.
Have you heard? The old scroll-keeper wants a book brought back from {place}.
Back and forth across the village with that hip? Somebody should save the walk.
{client}'s cat hasn't come home in two nights.
It was last seen near {place}, prowling the drying racks. Somebody should look.
The little dog from the corner house is gone again. Slipped its rope.
It always ends up somewhere it can't get back from. Poor thing.
{neighbor}'s ninken pup got out of the yard this morning.
A pup that young won't find its way home. Someone with a good nose, or a dog with one, should search.
{client} works late at the bath house and walks home past {place} in the dark.
Not a nice road at night. I'd feel better if somebody walked along.
{client} has to take the cart to the gate before dawn tomorrow.
Alone, with all those crates? I'd want someone walking beside me.
{client}'s mother has a fever, and the medicine is all the way at the hospital.
And {client} can't leave the bedside. Someone should fetch it.
{neighbor}'s grandfather has had that cough a week now.
The herbalists by the hospital have a tea for it. Somebody needs to go and ask.
Stock keeps going missing from {client}'s shop. A little every night.
Rats, or something cleverer than rats. Someone ought to keep watch.
The delivery for {client}'s stall never turned up. It was due at noon.
It's probably stuck at the gate. Somebody should go and find out.
{client} wants to learn the trade at the forge, but the smith won't take on anyone new.
The smith listens to people who've worked there. A good word from the right person might do it.
{client} has been asking the tailor for an apprenticeship for a month.
The tailor says no to everyone. It'd take someone persuasive to change that mind.
The squid stall's short-handed tonight. Two helpers came down with colds.
On festival night? They'll never keep up with the queue alone.
There's a little one crying by the goldfish stall. Can't find their family.
Someone should help look. The crowd's too thick for a child to see over.
The farmer from the east fields broke a cart wheel by the gate. The whole load's stuck.
It's Market Day, of all days. Someone strong could help carry it in.
My grandma's basket's too heavy to carry back from the market. I tried. I really tried.
We should find someone bigger. Or two of us could hold a handle each!
Our kite's stuck on the roof of {place}. We can't reach it.
A shinobi could jump up there easy. Let's ask one.
{friend} lost a {item} somewhere between the market and {place}.
Again? Ask the stallkeepers. They see everything that falls.
Did you hear? {neighbor} dropped a purse at the bath house and nobody handed it in.
Somebody must have it. The attendants are always gossiping, they'd know.
{friend} is beside themselves. The {item} from their grandmother is gone.
Last time I saw it was at {place}. Somebody should ask there.
I left my {item} on a bench by the river, and now it's not there.
The ferryman sees everyone who sits on those benches. Try asking.
{neighbor} came home without a {item}. Swears it was in the basket at the grocer's.
Then someone at the grocer's knows where it went.
Have you seen a little wooden box with a crane carved on the lid?
No. Whose is it? {friend}'s? Somebody at {place} might have picked it up.
{friend} lost the key to the shop. Can't open up tomorrow without it.
Was it on that string round the wrist? It must have snapped somewhere near {place}.
The flute {neighbor} plays at the shrine every evening has gone missing.
The shrine's been so quiet. Somebody ought to look.
{friend}'s headband came off during training, and they can't find it anywhere.
A Genin without a headband? That's a long talk with the Mission Desk. Someone should search the training grounds.
A {item} turned up at the tea house. Nobody's claimed it.
I think it's {neighbor}'s. Someone should find out before the tea house sells it to the pawn shop.
Somebody's dropped a letter by the well. Still sealed.
Then it hasn't reached whoever it was for. That's worse than losing it.
{friend}'s lucky charm from the shrine went missing at the festival.
In that crowd? It could be anywhere. Though the mask stall picks up whatever falls.
{neighbor} misplaced the ledger for the month. All the accounts.
Last seen at {place}. If it's lost for good, it's a whole month of sums to redo.
I'm sure I left my {item} on the counter at Ichiraku.
Then ask at the stand. Or ask whoever was on the next stool.
{friend} lost a whole spool of ninja wire near the training grounds.
Somebody'll trip on that. Better find it before a child does.
I lost my spinning top. The red one. It rolled away by {place}.
Maybe the big kids took it. Or maybe it's under the steps. Let's ask someone.
My little brother lost his marbles. Like, actually lost them. All of them.
I saw marbles near {place} yesterday! But I don't know whose they were.
I dropped my lunch money somewhere and now I'm going to starve.
You won't starve, you ate three buns this morning. But we should look.
Somebody took my practice kunai from the Academy yard.
Maybe somebody just borrowed it? Let's ask around the yard tomorrow.
I lost the hair ribbon my aunt gave me. She's going to ask about it.
Did you have it at {place}? Let's go back and look.
There's a new family in the house by {place}. Moved in three days ago.
I've not seen them out once. Someone ought to say hello.
The new tenant on the second floor keeps to themselves.
New to the Leaf, I heard. Doesn't know a soul. That's a lonely way to start.
Someone's moved into the empty shop on the corner.
A weaver, from a village down the east road. Doesn't know where anything is yet.
That new face at the tea house, every afternoon, always alone.
Moved here last week, I think. Somebody should show them round.
The new carpenter at the Kinoshita yard asked me where the market was.
The market! Imagine not knowing the market. Somebody needs to give them a proper tour.
A new family on our lane, and the children haven't made a single friend yet.
The Academy's hard when you start late. Someone could introduce them.
{neighbor} says the new healer at the hospital eats every meal alone.
Somebody should take them to Ichiraku. Nobody stays lonely at Ichiraku.
There's a new kid in our class. Sits by the window and doesn't talk to anyone.
Maybe they're shy. We could ask them to play at lunch?
The new kid on my street has a pet turtle. Nobody's even asked its name.
I want to know the turtle's name! Let's go say hi.
{friend} and {neighbor} haven't spoken in a week.
Over a fence, of all things. Someone they both trust should knock some sense into them.
Did you see {friend} cross the street to avoid {other}'s cousin?
They used to be inseparable. Whatever happened, it needs mending.
{friend} said something unkind at the tea house, and now {neighbor} won't come.
Both of them are too proud to say sorry first. Someone should carry the message.
{friend} and {neighbor} share a wall and won't share a word.
It's been like that since the festival. A silly thing that grew.
{friend} borrowed ryo from {neighbor} and paid it back late. Now neither will look at the other.
Late's not never. Someone ought to sit them down together.
The two stallkeepers by the bridge are shouting at each other again.
Over customers, as usual. It's bad for business, and bad for the street.
{friend} misses {neighbor}. Won't say it, but it's written all over that face.
Then someone should tell {neighbor}. Before it's too late to fix.
{friend} said I cheated at tag, and I didn't, and now we're not friends.
That's silly. You two always play together. Somebody has to make you make up.
{friend} and {neighbor} broke the kite together and now they both say it was the other one.
They won't sit together at lunch anymore. It's weird.
Our elder wants the old custom done properly this year. The gift at the gate, the right words and all.
Nobody remembers the right words. Someone would have to go and learn them from the elder.
The clan elder asked for the shrine at the clan hall to be tended, the old way.
That takes a whole day and a steady hand. The young ones are all on missions.
Our elder is upset. Nobody's brought the season's first fruit to the clan altar.
It's a small thing, but it matters to the old ones. Someone should do it properly.
The elder wants a guest to attend the clan rite. Someone from outside who honours it.
That's an honour, not a chore. Whoever does it will be remembered.
The elder wants the old feast dish made for the clan table. The one with seven kinds of root.
Nobody makes it anymore. Somebody would have to gather all seven.
The elder says the deer shrine in the forest needs fresh offerings. Hasn't been seen to since the thaw.
It's a long walk in. Someone patient should go.
The elder wants the first bloom of the year carried to the memorial. The old way, in both hands.
The greenhouse is too busy. Someone else will have to carry it.
The elder wants a gift for the old lead dog of the kennels. Proper respect, the way it used to be done.
A bone from the butcher and the right words. Someone should do it before the old dog's day.
Two clans glaring at each other over the market street again. It's getting ugly.
Nobody remembers who started it. Someone neutral should hear both sides.
Our clan elder refuses to sit in the same room as theirs now.
Over a boundary stone. A stone! Somebody needs to look at where it really stands.
The clan meeting ended in shouting. Their spokesperson walked out.
If it goes on, the whole district will take sides. Someone has to step between them.
Neither clan will buy from the other's shops anymore. The whole street's suffering.
Somebody outside both clans could carry a word. It has to start somewhere.
The Aburame say our dogs dug up their insect gardens again.
The dogs say nothing, as usual. Someone should go and see what really happened.
Their elder sent a letter. Very polite. Very cold. About the dogs and the hives.
Then it's serious. We need someone they'll listen to.
The kennel dogs trampled the beds behind the hive wall. A season's work, gone.
The Inuzuka will say it wasn't their dogs. Someone should look at the tracks before the rain does.
We should not raise our voices. But the gardens cannot go on like this.
Agreed. Someone from outside both clans should carry our words.
{friend} and {rival} sparred again this morning. Neither would stop when the bell rang.
Someone's going to get hurt. They need a referee, or a good talking-to.
Did you hear {friend} challenge {rival} in the middle of the mission hall?
The whole room went quiet. That's not friendly rivalry anymore.
{friend} has been training till midnight, just to beat {rival}.
That's not training, that's a grudge. Someone should talk sense to one of them.
They used to train together, {friend} and {rival}. Now they won't share a training ground.
A pity. They pushed each other well, back when it was friendly.
{rival} says {friend} cheated in the last spar. {friend} says {rival} is a sore loser.
And both of them are looking for a rematch. Somebody had better be there.
{friend} came home with a split lip from a "friendly" spar with {rival}.
Friendly. Right. Someone should make them shake hands before it gets worse.
I'm sick of it. {rival} keeps showing off at the training grounds, just to get at {friend}.
And {friend} keeps taking the bait. Someone needs to cool them both down.
The two of them are meeting at the training ground at dawn. "To settle it."
Settle what? It'll only make it worse. Someone ought to referee it, at least.
{friend} and {rival} had a race and both say they won and now they're going to fight.
A real fight? Someone should tell them it was a tie. It was nearly a tie.
{rival} keeps calling {friend} slowpoke, and {friend} threw a shoe.
It's getting silly. Someone big should make them stop.
